title: Progressive request throttling and safe snapshot replay for hosted API server-error waves
creator: Aisha Park
description: Summary: Several customers experienced multi-minute error waves (HTTP 500/502/504) around peak bursts last week. Root analysis indicates a feedback loop between aggressive client retries and an in-service autoscaler/queue pressure corner that amplifies backlog, causing GPU-side queue overflows and sporadic timeouts. This ticket implements a two-pronged mitigation: (1) progressive request throttling at the edge with per-tenant sampling to reduce retry amplification, and (2) a safe snapshot-replay mechanism on the runtime so that partially-processed in-flight batches can be retried without re-executing long prefixes or corrupting KV cache state.
acceptance_criteria: Edge layer exposes progressive throttling policy configurable per-customer with default safe sampling (5% -> 50% ramp) and immediate soft-429 behavior
Replay subsystem can reconstruct a deterministic lightweight snapshot for failed batches and resume from the last confirmed KV checkpoint without double-applying prefix state
End-to-end integration test reproduces a simulated peak with synthetic retries and shows 60% reduction in backend 5xx rate and 45% reduction in avg error burst duration
No detectable increase in successful-request latency under normal load (< 3% p95 change) after rollout
Instrumented dashboards show new metrics: request_sampling_rate, snapshots_replayed, replay_success_rate, throttle_applied_rate
rollout_plan: Step 1 (canary edge): Deploy progressive-throttler to edge pop in eu-west-1 with sampling default 10% for 24h
Step 2 (runtime canary): Enable snapshot-replay on 10% of dedicated GPU hosts that have hermetic sequence-length profiles for 24h
Step 3 (gradual ramp): If canaries stable, increase edge sampling to 25% and runtime replay to 33% over 48h; monitor replay_success_rate and p95 latency
Step 4 (customer opt-in): Expose a temporary customer toggle for high-impact tenants to opt-into aggressive protection (50% sampling + dedicated fastpath) while we validate
Step 5 (full rollout): Roll to all regions, default sampling 15%, and enable replay on all hosts behind a kill-switch for fast rollback
mitigation_steps: Immediate: Apply emergency soft-rate-limit (server-side 429) for top 5 noisy tenants to stop amplification while we deploy canary
Short term: Release hotfix to edge proxy to align SDK retry semantics (increase idempotency token checks and apply exponential-backoff with jitter)
Medium term: This ticket's progressive-throttling + snapshot-replay implementation
Communication: Notify affected customers with status updates and recommended client SDK update to avoid tight sync retries
telemetry_changes: Add metrics: edge.throttle.applied_by_tenant, edge.throttle.sample_rate, runtime.snapshot.size_bytes, runtime.snapshot.replay_duration_ms
New SLO alert: if replay_success_rate < 98% or throttle_applied_rate > 20% for >15m, page on-call reliability
Dashboard: error-wave heatmap (region x tenant) and pre/post comparison for canary windows
qa_tests: Chaos test: Synthetic client that retries at varying backoff distributions to validate that progressive throttling reduces peak backlog without increasing successful failure modes
KV integrity test: Run a suite that uses random prefixes and verify checkpoints match after replay across multiple seeds
Latency regression: Load test at 80% sustained capacity to ensure p95 increase <3%
Compatibility: Verify replay works with quantized model variants and both streaming and non-streaming RPC paths
